effort: Reorganize quickly after a small false step while preserving a high-quality exit.
brief: E2 uses a known lateral jab followed by a crossover exit. A two-foot-to-one-foot lateral landing controls an asymmetric receiving base, a short V shuttle links different corner types, two forward rebounds provide brief elastic force, a forward bound becomes a running exit, and a half-kneeling start isolates the initial lateral drive.
marker: For E2, record whether the jab leg accepts weight under control and the next crossover sends the body into the intended exit without an extra gather step; score both jab directions separately.
readiness: The jab is planned and small, not a reactive dodge against a defender. Confirm single-leg landing and comfortable floor-knee support; use conservative flight distances. Review actual fatigue from the linked routes rather than assuming that a new class number means recovery.
space: Use a measured 8 m × 6 m clear bay for the jab/diagonal exit and V route, including final stopping. Rebound and bound-to-run tasks use a single 10 m lane. Half-kneeling work needs a comfortable stable floor contact; do not require kneeling through discomfort.

drills.name: Two-Foot Lateral Jump to Single-Leg Landing
drills.execution: Push from both feet laterally within 0.3 m, land on the outside leg and hold 2 s; the free foot stays clear.
drills.job: Receive lateral force on one leg after a shared push, keeping the next foot free for an exit.
drills.layout: Clear 3 m × 3 m around the landing; mirror directions/landing legs, no approach.
drills.difference: Bilateral takeoff to unilateral landing, not a unilateral bound or a bilateral lateral landing.
drills.regress: Shorten the flight if the pelvis drops or the free foot must touch down.

drills.name: Planned Lateral Jab-to-Crossover Exit
drills.execution: From athletic stance, make a 0.5 m lateral jab, accept weight, then cross into the opposite forward diagonal for 2 m; stop over 2.5 m. The coach declares the whole route beforehand.
drills.job: Main force reversal after a small deceptive entry while avoiding extra foot gathering.
drills.layout: Mark the jab footprint and opposite diagonal exit. Keep the 4.5 m exit/stop and an empty escape area beyond the jab; mirror one route at a time.
drills.difference: A weight-bearing false step precedes an opposite-direction crossover exit; previous stationary crossover/drop-step starts did not reverse a jab's momentum.
drills.regress: Reduce jab width and speed if the athlete reaches outside the base or delays the exit with a hop.
drills.exposure: 1 travel redirection, jab braking and terminal stopping.

drills.name: V Shuttle to Opposite Diagonal
drills.execution: Run 1 m along one forward diagonal, reverse back 1 m to the start, then cut 90 degrees into the other diagonal for 1 m and stop over 2 m.
drills.job: Prepare a different second corner after a return rather than repeating one angle throughout a course.
drills.layout: Two 1 m diagonals form a right-angle V. Reserve final stop beyond the second arm and a clear abort corridor beyond the first cone; no extra return after the finish.
drills.difference: One 180-degree turn followed by a 90-degree exit at the shared origin; earlier multi-cut routes used repeated/alternating corner types without this return junction.
drills.regress: Lower speed on the return leg if the junction cut is late.

drills.name: Two Forward Rebound Jumps
drills.execution: Make two low forward jumps with an immediate controlled rebound after the first; hold the second landing 2 s. Each flight no more than 0.4 m.
drills.job: Express a second forward push after accepting force without a long pause.
drills.layout: Use two floor targets along the lane. Small hurdles may mark the same targets only if low enough for this flight; hurdle use does not create a new exercise. Clear 2 m beyond the final landing.
drills.difference: Whole-leg forward rebound with two flights, unlike ankle-only line hops or a forward jump ending in a hold.
drills.regress: Shorten both flights if the first landing sinks or the second requires a setup step.

drills.name: Single Forward Bound to Running Exit
drills.execution: Make one forward bound within 0.4 m onto the opposite leg, then run 1.5 m along the same heading; stop over 2.5 m.
drills.job: Let the first accepted contact feed the next forward running step without an extra jump.
drills.layout: Start near 2 m; bound, run 1.5 m and stop over 2.5 m, all within the lane. Flight distance is separate from the 1.5 m run ledger.
drills.difference: Forward flight continues into the same-heading run; the earlier lateral bound-to-run required perpendicular redirection.
drills.regress: Shorten flight and exit speed if the athlete needs a recovery hop.
drills.exposure: 1 unilateral landing and 1 terminal locomotor stop; no change of travel heading.

drills.name: Half-Kneeling Lateral Start
drills.execution: Start half-kneeling with the front foot aimed toward the exit; drive through it, bring the trailing leg through and accelerate 2 m laterally relative to the initial torso. Stop over 3 m.
drills.job: Create the initial exit force from the supported low leg position without relying on a preceding run.
drills.layout: Orient the front foot/run down the cleared lane, start near 2 m and finish stopping by 7. Choose the initial torso angle so the exit remains in the lane; floor-knee contact must be comfortable.
drills.difference: One knee and one foot provide the initial support, unlike standing, falling or hand-supported starts.
drills.regress: Use more upright torso and slower first step; defer the drill if comfortable knee contact or controlled rise cannot be established.
drills.exposure: 1 running initiation and terminal stop; no prescribed jump.

light.job: Keep the receiving leg controlled during asymmetric landings and the small jab.
Maintain active foot pressure while the jab changes the base.

strength.job: Maintain shared knee/hip force with a stable base as route density is reduced.
Retain hip-hinge strength for forward exit projection.
Retain lateral acceptance and push-back strength for the jab.
Support finishing hip extension in the short running exits.
Maintain adductor control while the jab shifts force sideways.
Maintain bent-knee ankle force without extra calf volume.

previous_review: Class 10 prescribed fourteen discrete cuts, four unilateral landings and nine primary bouts. No actual fatigue or performance data was supplied.
progression: Reduce discrete cuts to eight and keep each flight small. The new false-step and mixed-corner tasks apply prior qualities but do not provide a matched test of previous drills.
strength_progression: Keep one round per lift, familiar technical reserve and no automatic load increase. Use stable goblet squat and the already introduced hip thrust; omit the separate long-lever bridge this day to avoid unnecessary posterior-chain overlap.
audit: Rejected another lateral rebound-return pair because Class 2 already used it. Used a bilateral-to-unilateral landing instead. The V route has exactly two changes, and rebound work is two flights only; no extra finishing block.
next: Next class integrates the movement syllabus with new known routes, then audits all twelve prescriptions without claiming athlete gains or adding a repeated test.

light_entries.name: Lateral Step-Down — low support, light
light_entries.execution: Bodyweight first; a light dumbbell only if still easy. Lower **3 s**, lightly touch the free heel, return under control. Rest **30 s between legs; 45 s before S2**.
light_entries.regress: Rehearse the plant leg controlling knee travel and pelvic position during weight acceptance. Use the lowest stable support that permits a level pelvis and whole stance-foot contact; use hand support if needed. Reduce step height/load for knee collapse or pelvic drop.
light_entries.alternative: If the step is unsuitable, use instead a hand-supported shallow single-leg squat, the same 1 × 4 per leg and easy effort.
light_entries.job: Keep the receiving leg controlled during asymmetric landings and the small jab.

light_entries.name: Short-Foot Drill — supported standing hold
light_entries.execution: **5 s relaxed reset** between holds, **30 s between feet**, **60 s before P1**. Stand with most weight on the working foot and fingertip support.
light_entries.regress: Strengthen active arch control while maintaining heel, big-toe base and little-toe base contact for planting. Keep toes long; do not roll onto the outside edge. Use bilateral weight support instead if arch control needs toe-clawing or ankle rolling.
light_entries.job: Maintain active foot pressure while the jab changes the base.

strength_entries.name: Goblet Squat
strength_entries.execution: Dumbbell held close; lower 3 s through owned range and stand decisively with both feet grounded.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce load/depth if the trunk folds or heels lift.
strength_entries.job: Maintain shared knee/hip force with a stable base as route density is reduced.

strength_entries.name: Romanian Deadlift — two dumbbells
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; **2 s down**, purposeful hip extension; 2–3 RIR. Rest **120 s between working sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Maintain a softly bent, nearly constant knee angle, weights close and a controlled back position; stop lowering at the owned range.
strength_entries.job: Retain hip-hinge strength for forward exit projection.

strength_entries.name: Lateral Lunge — goblet dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: step out, lower **2 s**, push back to the original stance; 2–3 RIR. Rest **60 s between legs**.
strength_entries.regress: Keep the lunging foot grounded and knee aligned; sit into that hip without rotating away. Reduce width, depth or load for loss of control.
strength_entries.job: Retain lateral acceptance and push-back strength for the jab.

strength_entries.name: Hip Thrust — dumbbell
strength_entries.execution: Upper back on a stable bench, dumbbell secured over pelvis; rise to hip extension without arching the back, lower 2 s.
strength_entries.regress: Reduce load/range for lumbar extension or hamstring cramp.
strength_entries.alternative: If bench geometry is unsuitable, use instead a loaded dynamic floor glute bridge at the same rep/effort and preparation dose.
strength_entries.job: Support finishing hip extension in the short running exits.

strength_entries.name: Copenhagen Side Plank — short lever
strength_entries.execution: top knee/lower thigh on a stable bench, lower leg clear. Rest **60 s between sides**. Use bodyweight; if already controlled and too easy, secure a small dumbbell at the upper hip with the upper hand to reach the holding-effort target.
strength_entries.regress: Keep shoulder comfortable and pelvis level. Use light lower-foot assistance if needed; stop for groin/shoulder pain or loss of position.
strength_entries.alternative: If no suitable stable Copenhagen support fits, use instead floor side-lying hip adduction, upper foot on the floor in front, 1 × 8 per lower leg at 2–3 RIR with 60 s between sides; add a small hand-secured dumbbell above the inner knee only if needed and comfortable. Its preparation is 1 × 4 easy reps per leg instead of the hold ramps. This proposed replacement adds 16 dynamic working reps and removes 30 s of working holds; preparation adds 8 reps and removes 10 s of holds. Bouts are unchanged; allow up to 2 extra minutes.
strength_entries.job: Maintain adductor control while the jab shifts force sideways.

strength_entries.name: Bent-Knee Soleus Raise — seated, dumbbells on thighs
strength_entries.execution: bilateral; knees near 90°, forefeet on floor, **1 s at top, 2 s lowering, quiet bottom reset**; 2–3 RIR. Rest **90 s between sets**.
strength_entries.regress: Secure the weights above the knees, maintain knee angle and repeatable heel rise. Reduce load if heel height falls or bouncing replaces muscle force.
strength_entries.alternative: For seated calf work, use a securely held sandbag instead of dumbbells when its shape and load fit better.
strength_entries.job: Maintain bent-knee ankle force without extra calf volume.
